title: SetuGuard scorer-v2: feature pruning + holdout ranking gate

extraction.cache_integrity_check: 100% of 668 cache files parsed, filename sha256 == internal features.sha256, all expected feature keys present (0 corrupt)

skip_reasons.malicious_InvalidInstruction_39: androguard bytecode disassembler rejected obfuscated/corrupted DEX opcodes in cicmaldroid_banking samples
skip_reasons.malicious_AttributeError_1: FROZEN_FILE_FINDINGS.md Finding 1 (exported_components manifest node with no android:name -> NoneType.iter), known and deliberate, not fixed this session
skip_reasons.benign_EOCD_ValueError_7: fdroid_benign_apks files that are not valid ZIP archives (End of central directory record not found) -- data-quality issue in the corpus, not a scorer or memory issue
skip_reasons.benign_ManualTimeout_1: cash.p.terminal_243.apk, 172.2MB (the largest file in the entire 716-sample set by ~30x median). Killed after 300s wall-clock even when run alone with a dedicated 10G/8G/2G memory budget and zero contention from any other process. Not a scorer question; recorded as a known extraction-pipeline limitation.

extraction.operational_note: Initial 4-worker run under MemoryMax=8G/MemoryHigh=6G (no swap limit) caused system-wide swap exhaustion (8GB swap consumed, desktop starved) rather than the intended per-cgroup throttling, because MemoryMax/MemoryHigh do not constrain swap without a separate MemorySwapMax. Diagnosed and stopped (no cache corruption; per-APK immediate-write pattern held). A follow-up attempt with MemorySwapMax=0 caused a different failure mode (near-total stall under memory.high throttling with no swap relief valve for anonymous memory). Root cause of both was concurrency against a small number of atypically large APK files, not a general per-task leak. Resolved by splitting the remaining queue into 585 normal-sized files (processed with 2 workers, MemoryMax=8G/MemoryHigh=6G/MemorySwapMax=1G, completed in 704s at 1.20s/APK effective, 0 memory incidents) and 15 files >50MB (processed one at a time via harness/process_large_outliers.sh, each in its own scope with a dedicated 10G/8G/2G budget and a 300s hard timeout; 14/15 completed in under 60s each, confirming the earlier instability was concurrency-driven, not per-file; 1/15 (172.2MB) still timed out in isolation and was logged as a skip).

scorers.both: Pure functions over cached features dicts only; no Androguard re-invocation, no network, no Ollama.

score_distributions.note: n / mean / median / min / max / count-at-1.0-cap. Computed twice independently (harness/rescore_from_cache.py's stats() and a standalone statistics.median recompute) with identical results to 4 decimal places.

auc.method: Mann-Whitney U / rank-sum identity (exact, matches sklearn.metrics.roc_auc_score for the binary case); positive class = malicious, higher score = more suspicious
auc.verification: Direction verified on synthetic cases (positives-higher -> 1.0, positives-lower -> 0.0, all-tied -> 0.5) and cross-checked against an independent brute-force O(n*m) pairwise implementation on a random subsample (60 malicious vs all 16 holdout), which matched the rank-sum result to 4 decimal places (0.4589 both ways).

gate_malicious_vs_banking_holdout_16.interpretation: Both below 0.5: under both scorers, the average legitimate banking app still scores at or above the average malware sample. The new scorer narrows the gap (+0.0272) but does not cross 0.5.

gate_verdict_plain_sentence: Malware does not rank above legitimate banking apps under either scorer (AUC 0.3841 old, 0.4113 new, both <= 0.5 against banking_holdout_16); the three deletions improved the ranking gap without closing it.

determinism_check.method: Scored one cached feature set (harness/feature_cache/002ca15a26a80f025a45041df9bee5120653393c5ca41bdaca5f79ddda6d2731.json) three times with both _score_old and _score_new.

provenance_rule: Every number in the companion .md carries: corpus, n, seed (42), commit (46ce2ea=old, b3ff83b=new), cached-not-analyzed (all Task-4 numbers read harness/feature_cache/*.json only, zero re-invocations of Androguard), and which scorer (harness/rescore_from_cache.py:_score_old / _score_new) produced it.
